package_info.why_malicious: The report does not provide details about a specific malicious software package from a public package manager (such as npm, PyPI, etc.), but rather describes several attack campaigns, malware families, and vulnerabilities. Therefore, no single package can be analyzed at the package level.

execution_context.file_location: malicious macro embedded in Office document

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  ' Malicious macro code to drop and execute Loki.Rat'
  Dim objFSO, objFile
  Set objFSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
  Set objFile = objFSO.CreateTextFile("C:\Users\Public\loki.exe", True)
  objFile.Write <malware_binary_data>
  objFile.Close
  Shell "C:\Users\Public\loki.exe", vbHide
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the document is opened, the macro writes a malicious executable to disk and executes it, resulting in the installation of the Loki.Rat backdoor.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that write and execute binaries are a common malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents should not contain macros that drop and execute binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted environments (rare).

execution_context.file_location: malicious attachment or link in spear-phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the malicious attachment or link is opened, the code allocates memory, copies the Cobalt Strike beacon shellcode, and executes it, establishing a remote control channel.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Direct execution of shellcode is a hallmark of malware loaders.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate attachments should not execute arbitrary shellcode.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the app accesses device location and exfiltrates it to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltration of sensitive data to an untrusted server is a classic spyware behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Authentication apps should not send location data to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Location-based services (with user consent and transparency).

execution_context.file_location: injected JavaScript on compromised WordPress sites

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user visits the compromised site, the injected script causes the browser to send requests to a Ukrainian target, participating in a DDoS attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Websites should not force visitors' browsers to attack third-party sites.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not use visitors for DDoS.
key_indicators: Injected script sending requests to unrelated domains

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the ransomware uses IPv4 address-based obfuscation to hide shellcode, which is then deobfuscated and executed to download Cobalt Strike beacons.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation using IPv4 conversions is a novel anti-analysis technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate binaries do not obfuscate payloads in this way.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware reads environment variables for credentials and exfiltrates them to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Stealing credentials from environment variables and exfiltrating them is a classic info-stealer behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not exfiltrate credentials.

attack_chain.action: Victim receives spear-phishing email with malicious attachment or link.
Malicious macro or loader executes, dropping and running malware (Loki.Rat, Cobalt Strike).
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of remote access or control channel

attack_chain.action: Malware exfiltrates sensitive data or enables further attacks (info-stealing, lateral movement).
Compromised websites inject malicious scripts to conscript visitors into DDoS attacks.
Ransomware or advanced malware uses obfuscation and downloads additional payloads (Cobalt Strike).

behavioral_signatures: Office macros writing and executing binaries
Android apps exfiltrating location data to unknown servers
Injected JavaScript causing browsers to send unsolicited requests
Obfuscated shellcode using IPv4 address conversions
Malware reading environment variables for credentials and exfiltrating them
file_indicators: Unexpected executable drops in user directories
Injected scripts in WordPress site source code
network_indicators: Connections to known C2 domains (e.g., malicious.example.com)
HTTP POST requests to unknown or suspicious endpoints
Unexpected outbound traffic from Office or authentication apps
Browser traffic to DDoS target domains from unrelated sites
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that write and execute files, detect in-memory shellcode execution, flag Android apps exfiltrating sensitive data, scan websites for injected JavaScript making unsolicited requests, identify binaries using novel obfuscation techniques, and alert on processes exfiltrating environment variables or credentials to external servers.
